data.completion_memo: Implemented the task-16 format through the shared factory: canonical UUID records/foreign references, deterministic encoding and tombstones; disposable in-memory SQL projection covering all authoritative schema-14 domains; content-derived guarded writes, original-fingerprint receipts, cross-process file locking and prepared before/after journal recovery; local-only machine mappings/intents/QA ownership, portable receipt barriers; strict schema/merge/reference/SVG/model checks and external inventory invalidation. Desktop now compares full opaque cursors (native testing found numeric ordering skipped branch changes); QA uses returned guards, and retained history uses timestamps. Required completeness audit tightened local-change cursors, malformed draft/QA evidence checks, alias/tombstone collisions, and uncertain outcomes after journal preparation. Validation: 193 application tests pass (5 existing ignored), 8 focused text cases pass, frontend/native/MCP builds pass, two independent MCP processes pass concurrent writes and exactly-once QA replay, resolver/read-stability checks pass, and all 6 native Tauri/WebView2 text scenarios pass. Final evidence: target/native-storage/1fbc5e87-de98-46a3-ad5d-68911b59df3d/evidence.json and target/storage-parity/9136a17e-c609-4cef-a586-c2a64e5a8a0d/prepare-evidence.json. Contract, reproducible checks and filesystem/Git concurrency limitations are documented in docs/storage-text-format.md and docs/storage-text-validation.md. Task 18 can now add verified conversion and project settings.

Execution order: step 07 of 13. Depends on Adashi task ID 16. Complete this prerequisite before starting.

Phase: Git-friendly text storage implementation.

Implement the format and identity decisions from task 16 through the shared adapter:
- Support all authoritative project domains and their relationships, with stable IDs and deterministic, narrowly scoped file updates.
- Implement guarded writes, consistent reads, local cross-process coordination, idempotent operations, atomic multi-file change publication and recovery from interruption.
- Rebuild optional local indexes/caches from canonical files; they must never become a second source of truth.
- Detect external edits, Git checkout/pull/merge and branch changes; invalidate stale snapshots and notify desktop/MCP through the shared change mechanism. Preserve unsaved desktop edits and return actionable conflicts.
- Reject malformed data, unsupported schema versions, unresolved Git markers and semantic conflicts before allowing dependent writes.
- Keep the normal Git workflow under user control; the adapter reads/writes project files without automatically committing, pushing or resolving conflicting edits.

Acceptance: both desktop and MCP can read and mutate a text-backed project with the same domain behavior as SQLite. Independent edits touch only relevant canonical files, no-op reads leave the working tree clean, and interruption/conflict tests show no partial visible mutation or silent overwrite.

data.title: Storage 07/13 — Implement the Git-friendly text storage adapter
